aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Cross-Cohort Meta-Analysis of Socioeconomic and Lifestyle Determinants of Hypertension
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: Educational attainment, marital status, BMI, cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, and diet quality (fruit/vegetable intake, fat use) are independently associated with self-reported hypertension, and effect sizes are replicable across diverse cohorts differing in geography, race/ethnicity, and recruitment strategy.
concepts: Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary Yes/No
Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)
Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
Number of cigarettes smoked per day (average or current)
Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (beer, wine, liquor, other) per typical week, in standard servings
Frequency/servings of fruit consumption
Frequency/servings of vegetable consumption
Frequency/amount of butter, margarine, or fat used on vegetables, bread, or potatoes
Current marital/partner status of participant (categorical)
Participant's age in completed years (numeric value)
Sex of subject/participant (general, binary)
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Logistic regression within each cohort adjusting for age and sex, followed by random-effects meta-analysis across cohorts to pool odds ratios and assess heterogeneity (I²); sensitivity analyses stratifying by sex and education tertile.
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Harmonization of hypertension, BMI, smoking, alcohol, diet, educational attainment, and marital status across AI-READI, CLSA, and MESA with consistent CDE definitions enables a properly pooled multi-cohort regression and meta-analysis that was previously impossible due to non-uniform variable coding.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Pooled Prevalence and Cross-Cohort Comparison of Depressive Symptom Burden by Sociodemographic Subgroups
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: The prevalence and severity of CES-D-measured depressive symptoms vary systematically by age, sex, educational attainment, marital status, and BMI, and these gradients are consistent (or heterogeneous) across cohorts with different population compositions.
concepts: CES-D individual item — self-reported frequency of specific depressive symptom in past week
Participant's age in completed years (numeric value)
Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)
Current marital/partner status of participant (categorical)
Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
Sex of subject/participant (general, binary)
Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (beer, wine, liquor, other) per typical week, in standard servings
Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary Yes/No
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Compute item-level and summed CES-D scores within each cohort; estimate age- and sex-standardized prevalence of clinically meaningful depressive symptoms; apply Poisson or negative-binomial regression within cohorts and pool estimates via fixed- and random-effects meta-analysis; conduct subgroup analyses by marital status and education.
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Harmonization of the CES-D item CDE alongside sociodemographic and health variables across three cohorts now allows a properly standardized pooled prevalence estimate and subgroup meta-analysis of depression burden at a scale not achievable within any single cohort.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Mediation Analysis of Neighborhood Recreation Access on BMI and Cardiometabolic Outcomes via Physical Activity Proxies
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: Access to free or low-cost neighborhood recreation facilities is associated with lower BMI and reduced hypertension prevalence, and this association is partially mediated through behavioral pathways (fruit/vegetable intake, fat consumption) and moderated by educational attainment and marital status.
concepts: Neighborhood built environment and recreation facilities
Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
Waist circumference measurement in cm
Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary Yes/No
Frequency/servings of fruit consumption
Frequency/servings of vegetable consumption
Frequency/amount of butter, margarine, or fat used on vegetables, bread, or potatoes
Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)
Current marital/partner status of participant (categorical)
Participant's age in completed years (numeric value)
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Causal mediation analysis (Baron-Kenny framework with bootstrapped confidence intervals or counterfactual g-computation) within each cohort, with neighborhood recreation as exposure, BMI/waist circumference as outcome, and dietary variables as candidate mediators; moderation by education and marital status tested via interaction terms; results compared across cohorts for replication.
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: The simultaneous harmonization of neighborhood built environment, dietary intake variables, anthropometric measures, and hypertension across AI-READI and MESA with matching CDEs enables a formal mediation framework linking environmental exposures to cardiometabolic outcomes that required consistent operationalization of all mediator and moderator variables.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Cross-Cohort Replication of Cumulative Tobacco Exposure Metrics in Relation to Stroke and Cancer
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: Cumulative tobacco exposure (lifetime smoking indicator, years smoked, daily cigarette count, and non-cigarette tobacco use) is positively associated with stroke and cancer history, and these associations replicate across cohorts with distinct demographic compositions.
concepts: Lifetime ≥100 cigarettes smoked indicator (Yes/No)
Total years smoked cigarettes
Number of cigarettes smoked per day (average or current)
Self-reported clinician-diagnosed stroke (Yes/No)
Cancer diagnosis history (any type) – binary Yes/No indicator
Participant's age in completed years (numeric value)
Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)
Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (beer, wine, liquor, other) per typical week, in standard servings
Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Logistic regression of stroke and cancer outcomes on a composite pack-year proxy (daily cigarettes × years smoked) and lifetime smoking indicator within each cohort, adjusting for age, BMI, education, and alcohol; random-effects meta-analysis across cohorts; dose-response modeled with restricted cubic splines.
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Harmonization of three complementary tobacco exposure CDEs (lifetime indicator, years smoked, daily amount) alongside stroke and cancer outcomes across AI-READI and CLSA allows construction of a cumulative exposure variable and its replication across cohorts for the first time under a unified coding scheme.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Pooled Cross-Cohort Prevalence of Asthma and Association with Tobacco and Adiposity across Three Cohorts
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: Doctor-confirmed asthma prevalence differs across cohorts and is positively associated with BMI, cigarette smoking burden, and alcohol consumption, after adjusting for age, sex, and education.
concepts: Doctor-confirmed asthma diagnosis — subject, binary Yes/No
Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Age- and sex-standardized asthma prevalence estimated in each cohort; logistic regression of asthma on BMI, smoking, and alcohol within each cohort; random-effects meta-analysis to pool associations; Cochran Q and I² to quantify heterogeneity; BMI modeled as continuous and as category (CLSA/MESA overlap).
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Asthma diagnosis, BMI, smoking, and alcohol use have now been harmonized with consistent CDEs across CLSA, MESA, and UKBB, enabling a three-cohort pooled analysis with adequate statistical power to detect modest associations that individual cohorts might be underpowered to resolve.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Cross-Cohort Analysis of Educational Attainment as a Moderator of Diet Quality on Adiposity Outcomes
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: The magnitude of the inverse association between diet quality (fruit/vegetable intake, dietary fat use) and adiposity (BMI, waist circumference) is moderated by educational attainment, such that lower education attenuates or reverses the protective effect of diet; this moderation pattern replicates across cohorts.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Multiple linear regression of BMI and waist circumference on diet quality scores (summed from fruit, vegetable, and fat frequency variables) with education × diet interaction terms, estimated within each cohort; meta-analysis of interaction coefficients across cohorts; stratified analyses by marital status.
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Harmonized dietary intake variables (fruit, vegetable, fat frequency), adiposity measures, and educational attainment across AI-READI, CLSA, and MESA now permit a formal test and replication of education-as-moderator of diet–adiposity relationships at population scale.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Peripheral Arterial Disease Screening Metric (Claudication) in Relation to Cardiometabolic and Smoking Burden: Cross-Cohort Association Study
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: Exertional leg pain consistent with claudication is positively associated with cumulative cigarette exposure, hypertension, elevated BMI, and stroke history; these associations are detectable and consistent across two large independent cohorts.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Harmonization of the Rose/Edinburgh claudication questionnaire item alongside blood pressure readings, smoking burden, hypertension, stroke, and BMI across MESA and UKBB enables a replication study of peripheral arterial disease risk factors in two geographically and racially distinct populations under unified variable definitions.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.title: Sociodemographic and Behavioral Predictors of Self-Rated Health: Pooled Cross-Cohort Analysis with Mediation by Chronic Conditions
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.hypothesis: Educational attainment, marital status, BMI, smoking behavior, and alcohol use predict poor self-rated health, and a portion of this effect is mediated by diagnosed chronic conditions (hypertension, asthma, stroke, cancer), with effect sizes replicable across cohorts.

aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.method: Ordinal logistic regression of self-rated health (excellent to poor) on sociodemographic, behavioral, and chronic disease predictors within each cohort; causal mediation analysis decomposing total socioeconomic effect into direct and indirect (via chronic conditions) components; fixed- and random-effects meta-analysis of regression coefficients across cohorts.
aireadi_aou_clsa_mesa_ukbb.json.whyNewlyPossible: Self-rated health has been harmonized with the PhenX CDE across AoU, CLSA, and UKBB simultaneously with CDEs for chronic conditions, behavioral risk factors, educational attainment, and physical functional mobility, enabling a multi-cohort mediation analysis of socioeconomic pathways to subjective health that was not previously feasible with inconsistent coding.
